title: Identification of broadly tumour-reactive γδ TCRs from multiple myeloma.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Downloaded and opened all 8 files of the only public deposit (Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.20028241). README.txt states verbatim that the labels supplied are 'randomized tumor-reactivity labels' for a 200-cell subset, and that 'The full training data and/or PreGame models can be provided upon reviewer request'. Parsed PreGame_testing_labels.tsv (200 rows, one column, 166 zeros / 34 ones), PreGame_testing_matrix.feather (200 rows x 27 columns: cell-cycle scores, 21 genes such as GNLY, GZMB, TRDV1, and 5 antibody-derived CITE-seq markers), meta_discovery_tested.tsv (200 rows x 15 Seurat metadata columns, no reactivity label), and both Jupyter notebooks (a 100-member random-forest ensemble with SMOTENC oversampling). Searched NCBI GEO, BioProject, Europe PMC accessions and Zenodo for the underlying CITE-seq (cellular indexing of transcriptomes and epitopes by sequencing) data by topic and by author; found nothing matching.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Only the Europe PMC abstract was readable; the Nature full text is paywalled (no PMCID, isOpenAccess = N), so I could not read the Data Availability statement itself. The reported area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.864 for PreGame came from a web-search summary of the article page, not from text I retrieved, and is unverified.

a1_downloadable.note: FAIL, verified in the files. The only public artefact is a code + demo bundle on Zenodo whose README says the full training data is available 'upon reviewer request'. No GEO, SRA, BioProject, EGA or dbGaP deposit of the single-cell CITE-seq data was found by topic or author search.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: A 0/1 tumour-reactivity column exists (PreGame_testing_labels.tsv), but the README states these specific values are randomized, so no real label is publicly downloadable. The real labels come from a separate TCR-cloning and tumour-killing assay that is not deposited.

a3_inputs_present.note: For the 200 demo cells the 27 input features are present as numbers in the feather file; no identifier lookups needed. Only 200 cells, though.

a4_units_stated.note: No units or documentation anywhere. Columns are presumably Seurat SCT-normalised RNA counts and CITE-seq antibody-derived counts, but neither the README nor the notebooks say which, and 'Phase' is an undocumented 1/2/3 integer encoding.

a5_enough_rows.note: FAIL, counted in the file. 200 cells, 34 positives. The checklist floor is ~400 even for pure classification.

a6_fits_laptop.note: Entire public deposit is about 110 KB; the feature matrix is 26 KB. Trains in under 2 minutes per the README.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Cannot be checked. The paper is paywalled so no cell counts, patient counts or cohort sizes are retrievable to compare against the 200-cell demo.

a8_label_provenance.note: FAIL, stated in the README I read. The public labels are explicitly randomized placeholders, i.e. pure noise, not a measurement. The genuine labels are in-vitro tumour-reactivity assays on cloned γδ T cell receptors, which would be fine, but they are not released.

existing_models.name: PreGame (the paper's own random-forest ensemble for tumour-reactive γδ T cell receptors)
existing_models.score_and_split: A web-search summary of the article reports an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.864; I could not retrieve the paper text to confirm the number or the split. The training notebook sets up 10-fold stratified cross-validation but the released notebook never actually uses it, so the released code trains 100 forests on all data with SMOTENC oversampling and no held-out split.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Not retrievable: the discussion is behind the paywall.

existing_models.name: predicTCR (machine-learning classifier of tumour-reactive tumour-infiltrating T cells from single-cell RNA sequencing, Nature Biotechnology 2024)
existing_models.score_and_split: Reported to raise the geometric mean of sensitivity and specificity from 0.38 (earlier gene-set scoring) to 0.74 across tumour-infiltrating lymphocytes from several cancers; split details not verified by me. Code at github.com/ssciwr/predicTCR.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Not verified; I read only search summaries, not the paper.

existing_models.name: TRTpred / MixTRTpred (antigen-agnostic tumour-reactive T cell predictor, Nature Biotechnology 2024)
existing_models.score_and_split: Benchmarked against external datasets within a machine-learning framework; exact numbers and splits not retrieved by me.

backbone.name: scGPT or Geneformer (single-cell transcriptome foundation models) would be the natural backbone for cell-level tumour-reactivity prediction
backbone.hardware: Not assessable: the 200-cell demo carries 27 pre-selected features, not the full gene-by-cell count matrix a single-cell backbone needs.
backbone.licence: Zenodo record lists no licence at all, which is itself a reuse problem.

integration.partner_dataset: None usable. In principle VDJdb or the Adaptive/IMGT γδ T cell receptor repertoires could join on CDR3 sequence, but no T cell receptor sequences are present in the public deposit (only a clonotype ID column with no sequence).
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Cannot be written, because the public files contain no sequences, no patient identifiers and no real labels to join anything to.

controls.positive_control: None possible on the public data: with randomized labels, a working pipeline and a broken one both score at chance by construction.
controls.negative_control: Label shuffling is meaningless here because the released labels are already shuffled.
controls.external_validation: No second γδ T cell tumour-reactivity dataset was found in GEO, BioProject or Zenodo.

honest_claim_h3: On the public data the only honest claim is 'this code runs', since the 200 released labels are randomized and the real training set was never deposited.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use a T cell's gene and surface-protein profile to predict whether its receptor actually recognises tumour cells.
plain_idea.train_on: Each example would be one gamma-delta T cell from a cancer patient, described by its messenger RNA levels and roughly 5 antibody-measured surface proteins. Publicly I verified only 200 such cells; the real cohort size is unknown because the paper is paywalled.
plain_idea.predict: A yes/no call on whether that cell's T cell receptor kills tumour cells. The true answer comes from cloning the receptor into reporter cells and measuring activation or killing against tumour targets in the lab.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Cell-therapy groups currently clone and test receptors one at a time, which is slow and expensive; a reliable in-silico filter would let them pick the few worth testing. Gamma-delta receptors are especially attractive because they do not need matched tissue typing, so one receptor could in principle treat many patients.

more_or_better_data.why: We would have 200 cells with fake labels. predicTCR and TRTpred were each trained on real tumour-reactivity assays across multiple cancer types and are published with code.

confidence_score.why: With 34 nominal positives and randomized labels there is no replicate structure and no way to estimate per-prediction uncertainty.

models_beatable.why: PreGame itself cannot be reproduced without its withheld training set, and predicTCR (2024) and TRTpred (2024) are recent, externally benchmarked and in predicTCR's case openly coded.

guaranteed_improvement.why: The first condition fails outright: neither PreGame's weights nor its training data are available, so it cannot be run as our baseline and our model could not see everything it saw.

ml_idea: The project considered was to retrain or improve PreGame: predict, from a single gamma-delta T cell's transcriptome plus CITE-seq surface-protein readout, whether its T cell receptor is tumour-reactive, and compare a frozen single-cell foundation model (scGPT or Geneformer) plus a logistic head against the paper's 27-feature random forest. It is a reasonable idea and the underlying biology is valuable, but it is not executable on anything public.

effort.compute_note: Measured sizes directly: the whole Zenodo deposit is about 110 KB and the README states the demo trains in under 2 minutes. These numbers describe the toy demo, not the real task, which cannot be sized because its data is not released.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Read README.txt in the Zenodo deposit. It took one minute and says in plain English that the labels are randomized and the full training data is available only on request.

verdict_reason: Part A fails on four counts, all verified by opening the files. A1: the only public deposit is code plus a 200-cell demo, and its README says the full training data is available 'upon reviewer request'; no GEO, SRA, BioProject or EGA record exists. A8 and A2: the released tumour-reactivity labels are explicitly randomized placeholders, so there is no real target to learn. A5: 200 cells with 34 nominal positives is far below the ~400-row floor. A4: no units or column documentation. Revisit only if the authors later deposit the real CITE-seq matrix and assay-validated labels.
